geo.label: Fed on hold / tariff fog
parts: Macro Stance

The US mix is slower growth with sticky inflation, which keeps the Fed parked. Fourth-quarter GDP rose at a 1.4% rate, badly missing estimates, while inflation firmed to 3% [[n6879]]. January payrolls rose 130,000, beating forecasts, and unemployment fell to 4.3% [[n6226]]; Governor Waller says the March rate call depends on the labour market [[n7103]], so there is no near-term cut while jobs hold. AI earnings are strong, but macro is not delivering the rate relief multiples were counting on.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.45% and the 10Y at 4.05%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +60 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 8 bps and the 10Y 19 bps, a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more) that took 11 bps off the spread (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25). The curve is positively sloped and approaching, but still below, its long-run average, and bond traders see Fed cuts spilling into 2027 [[n7350]], so the long end has done the rallying. The S&P 500 closed at 6,946.13, down 0.47% over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 17.93 and the DXY at 97.70 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
New / Most Important

Trade policy, not the Fed, is the new shock. The Supreme Court ruling against Trump's tariffs is unlikely to end the trade-policy chaos [[n7312]]: a replacement global tariff started at 10% and the administration is working to lift it to 15% [[n7313]]. The path matters more than the level — uncertainty delays capex outside AI and keeps foreign investors questioning their US weight, while possible refunds are a one-off windfall for importers.
Playbook ✓

Own 5Y–10Y duration (IEF) while the 10Y stays below its 4.24% level of 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25): sub-2% growth caps long yields even with the Fed on hold [[n6879]]. Overweight the AI-capex chain and industrials, underweight consumer discretionary. What changes the call: a firm next payrolls print plus hotter inflation that lifts the 2Y back above 3.53% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25) — then cut duration and add banks.

geo.label: ECB on hold / recovery
parts: Macro Stance

Europe has the better macro mix. Eurostat confirmed euro-area inflation at 1.7% in January [[n2273]], leaving the ECB an easing option rather than a hiking risk, and European shares closed at a record high on an HSBC boost and easing AI-disruption fears [[n2288]]. The STOXX 600 finished at 633.47, up 4.1% over 20 sessions, against a 0.47% fall for the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
Activity & Inflation

February's PMI showed euro-zone businesses performing better than expected as manufacturing bounced back [[n2079]]; with inflation at 1.7% [[n2273]], that is a disinflationary recovery, the best mix for equity multiples. EUR/USD closed at 1.1775, down 2.02% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), easing pressure on exporters. The risk is that the factory bounce is restocking ahead of US tariffs rather than final demand.
New / Most Important

ECB leadership is now a market variable: economists expect Lagarde to exit early and hand the job to Knot [[n2261]], which markets would likely read as less dovish at the margin — more relevant for periphery spreads than for the rate path. The US tariff reset to 10% with a push toward 15% [[n7313]] keeps EU-US trade in limbo, with autos and luxury most exposed to any retaliation.
Playbook ✓

Stay overweight European equities versus the US, led by banks with wealth franchises and utilities, funded from US discretionary; the Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,173.32 is up 4.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). What changes the call: EU retaliation against US tariffs, a PMI that gives back February's rebound [[n2079]], or a succession fight that widens periphery spreads.

geo.label: targeted easing / weak credit
parts: Macro Stance

China is a consumer bounce layered on a still-deflating credit and property base, so we stay Mixed: tactically constructive on consumption and onshore equities, cautious on anything that needs credit growth. Tourism spending over the Lunar New Year hit a record $116 billion [[n0890]], a genuine demand signal. But one holiday does not repair household balance sheets hit by falling home prices, and the policy response so far is targeted rather than broad.
PMIs & Activity

The latest official read is January's manufacturing PMI, which dropped to 49.3 [[n0408]], still in contraction. The February PMIs are the next print, and the feed carries no fresh activity data beyond holiday spending [[n0890]]. A manufacturing reading back above 50 would confirm that the consumption pulse is broadening into production; a second sub-50 print would mark the holiday boost as a one-off. Our base case is a services-led stabilisation with manufacturing hovering near 50, which favours consumer names over industrials.
Credit Impulse

January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persisted [[n0552]], so the impulse reflects seasonal front-loading rather than a demand revival. Beijing is leaning on targeted measures such as city-level property relief [[n0836]] rather than broad stimulus, and the yuan's strength gives it room to do more. Without stronger household borrowing the credit impulse stays flat; what would change that is a February loan print that beats on household medium- and long-term loans, which the feed does not yet carry.
Property

New home prices extended their decline in January as weak demand hounded the sector [[n6347]]. Shanghai eased homebuying rules in the latest round of property relief [[n0836]]; easing in the largest tier-one market matters symbolically, but local relief has not yet stopped price declines, so we treat it as floor-building rather than a turn. Confirmation would be two consecutive months of narrowing new-home price falls, and until then developers and property-heavy banks stay underweight.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The US tariff regime was reset after the Supreme Court ruling [[n7312]]: a new global tariff started at 10%, with a push to 15% [[n7313]]. To the extent the new rate applies uniformly, it narrows China's relative penalty, a relative win for Chinese exporters. Industrial policy is aimed squarely at technology — China targets a five-fold increase in advanced chip output to meet AI demand [[n3297]]. The feed carries no new central fiscal stimulus figure; a consumption-support package building on the record holiday spending [[n0890]] is what would move us to Bullish.
Markets & Flows

The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,147.23, up 0.82% over 20 sessions, and ASHR at 34.57 is up 2.37%, while the Hang Seng sits at 26,765.72, up 0.06%, KWEB at 32.24 is down 10.19% and FXI is down 3.81% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). USD/CNY closed at 6.8831, down 1.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), with the yuan near a three-year high as US dollar uncertainty grows [[n0874]]. The split is clear: the onshore market and the currency are being bought, offshore internet platforms are being sold.
New / Most Important

The yuan is the story. Its move to near a three-year high [[n0874]] loosens domestic financial conditions, lifts the dollar value of onshore earnings for foreign holders and gives the PBOC room to ease without currency pressure. The tech push is the second leg: the planned five-fold expansion in advanced chip output [[n3297]] targets exactly the AI bottleneck that has driven global semis. That argues for owning onshore hardware and equipment suppliers and for treating foreign chip-tool vendors' China revenue as a multi-year risk.
Playbook ✓

Own the onshore leg through ASHR rather than KWEB — ASHR is up 2.37% over 20 sessions while KWEB is down 10.19% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — and keep a modest long-CNY position while USD/CNY trends lower. Avoid mainland developers until new-home price declines narrow [[n6347]]. Upgrade to Bullish on a February manufacturing PMI above 50 plus a loan beat; downgrade to Bearish if Beijing retaliates against the new US tariff. ⚠ Divergence: traders are piling into bearish yuan bets to hedge downside risks [[n0881]] even as spot sits near a three-year high — the options market does not trust the rally.

geo.label: hike bias / weak yen
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is the cleanest reflation trade in developed markets: record equities, a weak yen and a central bank still leaning toward tightening. Governor Ueda flagged a chance of a rate hike in March or April in a Yomiuri interview [[n3274]]. The political counterweight is real — in a surprise move the government tapped two reflationists for the BOJ board [[n3239]] — but that slows the pace of hikes rather than stopping them.
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 155.88, up 2.25% over 20 sessions, and the Nikkei 225 at 58,583.12, up 10.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The weak yen is doing more for equities than domestic growth: Q4 GDP grew an annualised 0.2%, below expectations [[n3110]]. The reflationist board picks [[n3239]] pushed the yen lower again, flattering exporters' earnings but testing the BOJ's tolerance.
Playbook ✓

Stay long Japanese equities, tilted to exporters and banks: a weak yen lifts translated earnings, and a March or April hike [[n3274]] widens bank margins. Hedge half the currency exposure. What changes the call: USD/JPY pushing well above 155.88 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) into intervention territory, which would trigger a sharp yen squeeze and an exporter sell-off, or the BOJ skipping both meetings as the new board members dilute the hawks.

geo.label: hiking bias / sticky inflation
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is the developed market where the next policy move is still up. January's core inflation hit a 16-month high, raising bets on a May rate hike [[n6656]]. Governor Bullock says she does not think inflation is taking off again [[n0256]], but with core inflation still rising, households face the risk of higher mortgage costs into mid-year — a headwind for domestic demand and rate-sensitive equities.
Demand & Financing

AUD/USD closed at 0.7061, up 0.93% over 20 sessions, and the S&P/ASX 200 at 9,128.30, up 2.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Corporate Australia is cutting labour costs: WiseTech plans to slash 2,000 jobs as AI ends the era of manually writing code [[n0263]]. Job cuts at a software leader alongside sticky core inflation is a stagflation-lite mix for domestic demand, and we expect resources and banks rather than rate-sensitive sectors to carry the index.
Playbook ✓

Underweight rate-sensitive domestic cyclicals and A-REITs; express Australia through the AUD and resources instead, where a strong currency and a firm RBA reinforce each other. Trigger to turn Mixed: a softer next monthly CPI that takes the May hike [[n6656]] off the table. Risk to the AUD long: a US-Iran escalation that hits global risk appetite.

geo.label: easing cycle / strong growth
parts: Monetary & Activity

Poland pairs fast growth with on-target inflation. GDP growth accelerated to 4% (PKB przyspieszył do 4 procent — 'GDP accelerated to 4 percent') [[n3554]], and January CPI landed in the target band, though above forecasts, with economists assessing the chances of a March rate cut (inflacja w celu, ale powyżej prognoz — 'inflation on target, but above forecasts') [[n3567]]. The risk is that the upside surprise persuades the RPP to pause.
FX & Markets

EUR/PLN closed at 4.2139 and USD/PLN at 3.5790, up 2.48% over 20 sessions on dollar strength (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). EPOL rose 2.0% to 38.71 in the prior session and the Beta ETF WIG20TR closed at 69.17, up 2.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Leaders: KGHM at 342.00, up 13.17% over five sessions, plus Orlen (PKN) at 115.10 and Pekao (PEO) at 233.40, up 9.66% and 7.86% over 20 sessions; CD Projekt at 249.00 is down 12.82% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
Companies

Orlen plans to inject 5.1 billion zlotys into utility unit Energa [[n3428]], strengthening the group's grid and generation investment capacity. KGHM is the market's lever on copper, which closed at 5.98, up 2.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — the purest Polish exposure to the AI data-centre and grid metal. PKO at 93.58 and PZU at 69.90 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) anchor the dividend trade alongside Pekao.
Security & New Development

Poland, Germany, France, Italy and the UK will jointly develop low-cost air-defence systems [[n3406]], which keeps defence and engineering order books full. The bill is fiscal: the European Commission warns Poland's debt is on track to breach 100% of GDP by 2036 [[n3425]]. That caps how far Polish government bonds can rally even as the RPP eases, and it makes the zloty more sensitive to any fiscal slippage headline.
Playbook ✓

Stay overweight Poland via EPOL or the WIG20TR ETF, with PKO, Pekao and KGHM as core holdings; add on a March rate cut that leaves the zloty stable. What changes the call: a hawkish RPP hold, EUR/PLN breaking sharply higher, or fiscal slippage. ⚠ Divergence: house prices recorded their first annual fall since 2013 [[n3413]] — a turning property cycle sits awkwardly with a bank-led equity rally.
Narrative

Consensus spent February pricing an 'AI scare' against software: XLK is down 3.4% over 20 sessions and MSFT 16.64% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is whether AI partners with incumbents or replaces them; Nvidia's Jensen Huang says markets 'got it wrong' on the threat to software [[n5417]].
Reported

Salesforce beat and committed $50 billion to buybacks [[n1803]], while Workday hit a more-than-five-year low as a sluggish sales forecast sparked AI-disruption fears [[n5465]]. The market's test is the forward subscription guide, not the quarter.
EPS Upside Watch

Hardware and chip-design software tied to AI build-outs: Nvidia's earnings and guidance beat, with data-centre revenue up 75% [[n5411]], feeds straight into server and networking demand. Seat-based software is where expectations are lowest, so in-line guides can now surprise.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The contrarian trade is the crowded short in large-cap software: if Huang is right [[n5417]], MSFT at 400.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) prices disruption that has not reached its numbers, while Workday's slide [[n5465]] shows the risk is real for narrow, seat-based vendors rather than platforms.
Narrative

Communication services are flat: XLC is down 0.34% over 20 sessions, META closed at 653.69 and GOOGL is down 6.47% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is capex versus ad returns — Meta struck an AI chip deal with AMD days after committing to deploy millions of Nvidia GPUs [[n5056]].
Reported

The Trade Desk slid after earnings as its growth slowdown unnerved Wall Street [[n7387]], a warning for programmatic ad spend outside the walled gardens. Netflix rose 5.97% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Platforms with their own AI inference capacity should keep taking ad budgets from independent ad-tech [[n7387]]; Meta has estimate upside if second-sourcing chips from AMD [[n5056]] lowers its compute cost per ad dollar.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus treats Big Tech capex purely as a cost; multi-vendor chip deals show the largest buyers gaining pricing power over suppliers — a margin positive that is not in estimates, so we would not short the platforms on capex headlines alone.
Narrative

Financials are split between strong bank earnings and a private-credit scare: XLF is down 2.13% over 20 sessions, though BAC rose 2.54% and JPM 2.02% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Bloomberg reports private-credit fears deepening with a UBS warning of 15% defaults [[n5517]].
Reported
HSBC was the reporting standout, lifting European shares to a record close [[n2288]]; in the US the sector is trading private-credit headlines rather than fresh earnings [[n5517]].
EPS Upside Watch

Money-centre banks with trading and wealth franchises: volatility and capital-markets activity support fees even as a flatter curve trims margins. GS at 921.38 rose 2.12% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The contrarian signal is geographic: HSBC's results drove European shares to a record [[n2288]] while US financials trail. Global banks with wealth franchises are re-rating and US alternative managers and BDCs are de-rating — own the former, avoid the latter until private-credit marks settle.
Narrative

Energy is the year's leadership trade: XLE is up 10.47% over 20 sessions, Brent closed at 70.85 and WTI at 65.42 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is the Iran risk premium — Trump set a 10–15 day deadline for a deal or 'bad things' [[n2664]].
Reported
EOG beat profit estimates on strong output and higher gas prices [[n5120]]; XOM at 149.06 and CVX at 184.22 are up 8.94% and 8.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Upstream oil producers carry the most estimate upside if Brent holds, because consensus was built on lower prices; gas-weighted names are the exception, with Henry Hub at 2.97, down 57.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Supply is loosening under the geopolitics: OPEC+ is considering a 137,000 bpd output increase for April [[n5488]]. An Iran deal would leave rising supply and no premium — hold the sector with Brent puts.
Narrative

Industrials are the AI-capex beneficiary with real earnings: XLI is up 6.39% over 20 sessions, CAT 19.99% and GE 15.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Consensus is right on direction but too narrow — the demand story is broadening from data centres into construction and farm equipment.
Reported

Deere boosted its outlook and sees construction and small-agriculture demand recovering [[n1565]]; Axon jumped 17% after results [[n7393]]. Both were rewarded for lifting forward guidance, not merely beating.
EPS Upside Watch

Machinery and power equipment: Deere's recovery call [[n1565]] suggests the agriculture and construction cycle is bottoming on top of data-centre power demand. CAT at 766.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) is the cleanest combination of both, and its estimates still embed a flat construction cycle.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Aerospace is not participating: BA at 230.36 is down 5.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) while machinery leads. The industrial upswing is a capex story, not a travel or defence-prime story, so pair longs in machinery against aerospace underweights.
Narrative

Discretionary is the weakest cyclical: XLY is down 4.56% over 20 sessions and AMZN 13.91% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is a cautious middle- and lower-income consumer, compounded by AI-capex fatigue at the sector's largest weight.
Reported

Home Depot topped estimates for the first time in a year but said project demand remains muted [[n1724]]; Lowe's dipped 4.2% despite its beat [[n7393]]; TJX forecast muted annual sales and profit as consumers curb spending [[n1784]]. Housing-linked retail is being priced on volumes, not beats.
EPS Upside Watch

Home improvement on a lag: US mortgage rates reached their lowest since 2022, boosting refinancing [[n6724]], and refinancing tends to fund home projects with a delay. HD at 375.57 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) is the name to own first if housing turnover confirms.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Retail is buying what institutions sell in Tesla [[n4006]], which keeps TSLA at 417.40, down only 3.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), while the rest of discretionary de-rates — the sector's largest single-stock risk now sits with retail holders.
Narrative

Staples are the crowded defensive: XLP is up 7.03% over 20 sessions and WMT 7.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), and 24/7 Wall St. counts consumer staples up almost 20% while the S&P 500 struggles [[n7405]]. The rally is rotation into safety, not an earnings upgrade cycle.
Reported

Diageo fell nearly 13% after slashing its dividend and lowering its profit outlook [[n2290]] — the defensive label does not protect against volume declines. COST slipped 0.37% in the prior session to 994.76 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Scale value retailers — Walmart, Costco — have the cleanest estimate path, but after a near-20% sector rally [[n7405]] the upside is in the price. Branded food, beverages and spirits face negative revisions as volumes weaken and promotions rise.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Novo Nordisk plans to halve the US list price of Wegovy from 2027 [[n5273]]; cheaper GLP-1 drugs widen the volume threat to snack and beverage makers just as their multiples peak. Defensive money is crowding into the part of staples most exposed to that shift.
Narrative

Healthcare is a policy story: XLV is up 1.53% over 20 sessions while LLY closed at 1,028.83, down 1.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). CMS Administrator Oz says most-favoured-nation drug pricing will become the standard [[n5585]], which caps pharma multiples.
Reported

Pharma reporting in the feed window was thin; the sector's defining announcement was Novo Nordisk's plan to halve the US list price of Wegovy from 2027 [[n5273]]. That moves the obesity category from volume-led growth toward price competition.
EPS Upside Watch

Managed care rather than pharma: MFN pricing [[n5585]] shifts economics away from manufacturers and toward payers. UNH rose 3.74% in the prior session to 284.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), and lower drug list prices reduce benefit-cost pressure into the next guide.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The obesity franchise is turning into a price war: list-price cuts [[n5273]] put pressure on the category leader, and LLY is down 1.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) despite its dominance. Growth investors still treat GLP-1s as a duopoly volume story; the pricing data say otherwise.
Narrative

Materials are a metals trade: XLB is up 6.16% over 20 sessions, gold closed at 5,226.20 and copper at 5.98, up 2.59% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). J.P. Morgan sees gold at $6,300 by the end of 2026 [[n5638]].
Reported

Rio Tinto reported record copper and bauxite production for 2025 [[n4964]] — copper is now the growth engine for diversified miners. FCX at 68.82 is up 9.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Copper producers, as owners of the AI data-centre and grid metal: record output at Rio [[n4964]] and firm prices point to upward revisions for FCX and KGHM-type pure plays. Gold miners lag bullion — NEM is down 1.69% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — leaving margin upside if prices hold.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Silver is the warning: SLV is down 21.21% over 20 sessions despite a 14.2% five-session rebound (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), a reminder that precious-metal momentum can reverse violently even with a $6,300 gold call on the table [[n5638]].
Narrative

Real estate is benefiting from falling long yields: XLRE is up 5.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), and CNBC reports that dividend-paying real estate stocks are outperforming as AI fears roil markets [[n4903]].
Reported

REIT reporting in the feed window was light; the sector is trading rates, with the 10Y down 19 bps over 20 observations to 4.05% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25). XLRE closed at 43.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Residential and housing-adjacent REITs: mortgage rates at their lowest since 2022 [[n6724]] should lift transaction volumes and lower refinancing risk for leveraged landlords, which feeds funds-from-operations estimates with a lag.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Real estate is behaving as an AI hedge rather than a pure rate play [[n4903]]: investors are buying physical cash flows that software cannot disrupt. That bid can persist even if yields stop falling, which makes the sector more resilient than its rate beta suggests.
Narrative

Utilities are the AI-power trade: XLU is up 9.05% over 20 sessions and CEG 12.84% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Trump says he has told big tech companies to build their own power plants [[n5553]], putting generation at the centre of the AI build-out.
Reported
Constellation topped earnings estimates [[n7286]] and rose 10.81% over five sessions, while VST closed at 175.36, up 6.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Independent power producers with nuclear and gas fleets — CEG, VST — can sign direct supply deals with hyperscalers if behind-the-meter power becomes policy [[n5553]]. NEE at 95.11, up 9.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), offers the renewables leg.
⚡ Breaking Convention

'Bring your own power' cuts both ways: if hyperscalers self-supply, regulated utilities lose some of the load growth that justified their capex plans. The trade therefore favours generators over wires-and-pipes utilities, a split the sector ETF hides.
Narrative

European autos are a value trap: the STOXX autos tracker closed at 46.15, down 0.85% over five sessions, and VOW3 at 99.94 is down 4.0% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is weak European demand and the cost of the EV transition [[n4869]].
Reported
New car registrations fell 3.9% in January, with battery-electric cars at a 19.3% share [[n5161]], and Stellantis faces its first annual loss after EV write-downs [[n4869]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is scarce; the least-bad estimate path is at the premium end — BMW at 88.12 and Mercedes at 58.99 are up 1.29% and 2.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — but neither has a volume catalyst while registrations fall [[n5161]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Stellantis is the contrarian: STLA at 7.71 is down 20.92% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), so the write-down risk [[n4869]] is largely priced and any sign of a US sales recovery would meet very low expectations.
Narrative

Semis remain the AI earnings engine: SOXX is up 4.82% over 20 sessions, TSM 14.6% and ASML 4.94%, while AMD is down 16.34% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The memory boom is the new layer, leaving PC and smartphone makers in the cold [[n5475]].
Reported

Nvidia beat on earnings and guidance, with data-centre revenue up 75% [[n5411]]; TSMC raised its dividend 28% on 38% revenue growth [[n5407]]. Both confirm that AI demand is still accelerating at the foundry and accelerator level.
EPS Upside Watch

Memory and foundry: MU at 429.00 is up 4.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) with pricing power from the memory squeeze [[n5475]], and TSMC's dividend increase [[n5407]] signals management confidence in sustained AI demand.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The losers sit inside tech: memory costs are a margin hit for PC and handset makers [[n5475]], so the AI chip boom is a transfer from device makers to chipmakers rather than a tide that lifts all hardware. Pair chip longs with device-maker underweights.

earnings_pattern.title: Beats are table stakes; guidance and capital return get paid
parts: Rewarded

Companies that paired a beat with a raised outlook or visible demand: Axon jumped 17% [[n7393]], Deere boosted its outlook [[n1565]], Constellation topped estimates [[n7286]], and HSBC's results lifted European shares to a record [[n2288]]. Nvidia's earnings-and-guidance beat [[n5411]] extended the pattern into the AI supply chain.
Punished

Beats with soft guides were sold: Workday hit a five-year low on a sluggish sales forecast [[n5465]], Lowe's dipped 4.2% and GoDaddy slumped 16% [[n7393]], TJX's muted forecast weighed [[n1784]], and Diageo fell nearly 13% after cutting its dividend [[n2290]].
Pattern

The market pays for forward visibility and penalises two things: subscription models seen as exposed to AI substitution, and consumer companies guiding cautiously. Hard-asset and AI-infrastructure exposure is rewarded even at high valuations, while optically cheap consumer and software names keep de-rating on in-line numbers.
Attention into EPS

Attention shifts to the AI-infrastructure tail of the season: CoreWeave, where options traders expect a 15% move on its Q4 results [[n1748]]. Nvidia's forecast of accelerating growth [[n5418]] raises the bar for every AI-supply-chain report that follows, because in-line guides will now read as deceleration.
Playbook

Buy beats only with raised guides; fade beats paired with flat outlooks on the first bounce. Into prints, prefer companies with buyback capacity — Salesforce committed $50 billion [[n1803]] — and physical AI exposure over seat-based software. Change the call if two or more software names rally on in-line guides, which would signal the de-rating is exhausted.

underowned.title: Large-cap software after the AI scare — Microsoft
parts: Attention Gap

Morgan Stanley calls Microsoft the most under-owned stock [[n1530]], and MSFT is down 16.64% over 20 sessions to 400.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The AI-disruption narrative has been applied to the whole software complex, yet Huang argues the market got that threat wrong [[n5417]], and platform vendors own the distribution that AI agents need.
Exposure & Risk

Express through MSFT shares or a software ETF such as IGV, adding in stages and only after the stock stops making lower lows. Risks: new AI-agent launches that reignite the rout, Workday-style guidance misses spreading to larger vendors [[n5465]], and capex intensity weighing on free cash flow.

underowned.title: The refinancing window — housing-linked equities
parts: Attention Gap

US mortgage rates are at their lowest since 2022 and refinancing is picking up [[n6724]], but attention is on AI and the market still treats housing as frozen — Home Depot says project demand remains muted [[n1724]]. The 10Y is down 19 bps over 20 observations to 4.05% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25), which feeds into mortgage pricing with a lag.
Exposure & Risk

Express via HD at 375.57, down 1.26% over 20 sessions, and XLRE at 43.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), plus homebuilder ETFs such as ITB and XHB. Risks: a tariff- or oil-driven rebound in yields that closes the window, and households using refinancing savings to repair balance sheets rather than spend.

crypto.title: Short squeeze off the lows; stablecoins are the growth story
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 67,960.12, up 6.06% on the prior completed daily close and 8.39% over 20 days, while ether rose 10.88% to 2,054.63 and solana 11.23% to 87.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Equity proxies outran spot: COIN rose 13.52%, MSTR 8.86% and IBIT 7.39% in the prior session, though IBIT is still down 22.52% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
New / Most Important

The fundamental news is in stablecoins, not tokens: Circle reported $770 million of Q4 revenue with USDC circulation reaching $75 billion [[n1292]]. Even after the bounce, bitcoin is heading for its worst month since the crypto collapse of June 2022 [[n1186]], so the market is separating payment rails, which are growing, from speculative assets, which are still deleveraging.
Playbook

Treat bitcoin's rally as a squeeze until it clears the hurdle around $70,000 that CoinDesk flags [[n1249]]; above it, add spot or IBIT, and below the 20-day low cut risk. Prefer stablecoin rails — Circle, Coinbase — over spot beta, given USDC growth [[n1292]]. What changes the call: renewed ETF outflows or a risk-off shock from Iran.

flows.title: Duration bid, dollar steady, credit cracks in private markets
parts: Rates & Dollar

The DXY closed at 97.70, up 1.54% over 20 sessions but flat over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), so the dollar has stabilised rather than broken lower. The long end is bid: TLT is up 2.4% and IEF 1.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), consistent with a 10Y at 4.05% and a bull flattening (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25). BofA says US stocks drew their lowest share of global flows since 2020 [[n2373]].
Credit Check

Public credit is calm: HYG closed at 80.92, down 0.31% over 20 sessions, and LQD at 111.65, up 0.76% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The stress is private — Bloomberg reports a UBS warning of 15% defaults [[n5517]] — and it has not yet reached high-yield ETF prices. We read that as complacency rather than resilience: tight public spreads leave no cushion for a private-credit spill-over.
Portfolio Implication

Keep credit beta low: prefer LQD over HYG and avoid listed BDCs and alternative managers until private-credit marks settle. Own IEF/TLT as the hedge against an AI-capex or private-credit accident, and fund international overweights — Europe, Japan, Poland — from US discretionary, in line with the global flow rotation [[n2373]]. Change the call if HYG breaks lower on rising defaults or a strong payrolls print lifts the 2Y back toward 3.53% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25).

anticipatory.title: US–Iran nuclear talks in Geneva
parts: What Is Priced

The US issued new Iran sanctions on the eve of nuclear talks in Geneva [[n3011]], after Trump set a 10–15 day deadline for a deal [[n2664]]. Oil carries a premium — Brent closed at 70.85, up 4.85% over 20 sessions, and gold at 5,226.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — but the VIX at 17.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) says equities price a contained outcome.
Conditional Expression

If talks produce a framework, fade the premium: trim XLE, sell Brent upside and buy airlines and European cyclicals. If talks fail and strikes follow, own Brent call spreads, XLE and gold, and underweight airlines, oil-importing emerging markets and carry trades funded in low-yielders that suffer in risk-off.
Risk

The binary is not clean. OPEC+ is considering a 137,000 bpd increase for April [[n5488]], so a deal could push oil below pre-tension levels quickly, while a limited strike could spike prices only briefly. Size positions for a gap, not a trend, and prefer options to outright futures.

anticipatory.title: The Fed's March call — labour data decide
parts: What Is Priced

Bond traders have pushed expected Fed cuts into 2027 [[n7350]], and Waller says the March decision depends on the labour market [[n7103]]. The 2Y at 3.45% is only 8 bps lower over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25), so a March cut is not the base case.
Conditional Expression

If the next payrolls report disappoints, the 2Y has the most room to fall: own 2Y notes or a 2s10s steepener and add small caps — IWM closed at 264.58, down 0.06% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). If payrolls beat again after January's 130,000 [[n6226]], expect the 2Y to reprice higher and the dollar to firm; favour banks and energy over duration.
Risk

Inflation, not jobs, could decide: fourth-quarter inflation firmed to 3% [[n6879]], and tariff pass-through could keep the Fed on hold even with softer hiring. A hold with soft data would flatten the curve further and hurt small caps.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — beat-and-raise into the Vera Rubin ramp
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia's results beat on earnings and guidance, with data-centre revenue up 75% [[n5411]], and its forecast points to accelerating growth as Vera Rubin starts hitting the market [[n5418]]. Our thesis: supply, not demand, is the binding constraint into the Rubin ramp, which supports pricing and margins through the year and keeps hyperscaler capex flowing to Nvidia first.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVDA closed at 195.56 before the report, up 1.41% on the day and 3.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The hurdle is holding above that pre-report close: a beat-and-raise that cannot hold the level would say investors are fading AI capex regardless of results. Bullish while above 195.56; the call fails on a close back below it within a few sessions or on any sign hyperscalers are trimming orders.

catalysts.title: $CRWV — leverage meets the print
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CoreWeave's Q4 results are the next AI-infrastructure test, with options traders pricing a 15% move [[n1748]]. Our thesis: the reaction will hinge on funding costs and capex, not revenue, because the private-credit market that finances GPU fleets is under stress, with UBS warning of 15% defaults [[n5517]]. A revenue beat paired with higher interest expense would be sold.
Price Hurdle & Risk

CRWV is not on our market card, so no level is quoted. The risk to the short is Nvidia's accelerating guide [[n5418]], which implies scarce GPU capacity and pricing power for neoclouds; cover on faster backlog conversion with lower funding costs.

catalysts.title: $CEG — the 'bring your own power' winner
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Constellation topped earnings estimates [[n7286]], and the next catalyst is policy: Big Tech companies are to meet Trump at the White House to sign a pledge on data-centre power costs [[n5545]] after he told them to build their own power plants [[n5553]]. Nuclear fleets that can contract directly with hyperscalers are the cleanest beneficiaries of that shift.
Price Hurdle & Risk

CEG closed at 325.84, up 4.22% in the prior session, 10.81% over five sessions and 12.84% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). After that run, add only on pullbacks that hold the post-results gap; the call fails if the pledge shifts grid costs onto generators or if hyperscalers favour new gas builds over existing nuclear.

retail.title: Strategy / MSTR — the most-shorted bitcoin proxy
parts: Observed Attention

Goldman Sachs lists Strategy and Coinbase among the most-shorted stocks [[n1314]]. MSTR rose 8.86% in the prior session to 135.65 but is down 16.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
Motivation & Bias

Retail is playing for a squeeze: heavy short interest plus a bitcoin bounce is a classic setup. The bias is to treat short interest as fuel rather than as a hedge against bitcoin exposure, and the stock amplifies bitcoin in both directions.
Instrument & Risk

Prefer defined-risk call spreads to shares or leveraged single-stock ETFs; the trade works only if bitcoin clears the $70,000 hurdle [[n1249]]. Risk: bitcoin is still on track for its worst month since June 2022 [[n1186]].

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — retail buys what institutions sell
parts: Observed Attention

Retail investors are piling into Tesla as institutional investors sell [[n4006]]. TSLA closed at 417.40, up 1.96% in the prior session and down 3.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
Motivation & Bias

Loyalty and the autonomy narrative: retail treats institutional selling as a buying opportunity, a contrarian bias that works in squeezes but ignores fundamentals such as falling European car registrations [[n5161]].
Instrument & Risk

Prefer shares or long-dated calls over daily-reset leveraged ETFs in a choppy tape. Risk: if institutions keep distributing, retail becomes the marginal buyer at ever-higher conviction and thinner liquidity.

Express nuclear demand through earnings-backed generators — CEG closed at 325.84 and VST at 175.36 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — rather than pre-revenue reactor developers; if trading Oklo, use small option positions.
